minutes.headline: Committee presented its plan for a new grade 6-12 middle-high school at a public forum; no votes were taken.
minutes.summary: The third public forum of the School Building Committee laid out the case for a new combined middle and high school built beside the current high school. It covered the building's condition and accreditation risk, the options studied, the schedule, the project budget and state share, and the homeowner cost over a 30-year financing term. Residents asked about a greenhouse, solar panels and the cost of the alternatives. No votes were taken.

public_comment.topic: A resident and alumnus, parent of a fifth grader, said the tour showed the outdated chemistry lab and asked about a greenhouse shown in the plans.
A resident said they were disappointed the building has no solar panels and wanted a solar educational opportunity.
A resident spoke of the positive effect of new schools elsewhere and suggested selling the old 1950s fixtures.
A resident asked about the cost of a new high school only, the cost of keeping and repairing the current building if the project fails, and over what period.

budget_items.topic: Limited renovation of existing high school
budget_items.what_was_said: Bringing the building up to code was estimated as not reimbursable by the state building authority.
Renovate and add on option was estimated at a project cost that does not solve issues at the other schools.
Study was funded at one amount but the spend will be lower.
Presenter walked through design fees, construction manager, construction cost, miscellaneous costs, furnishings, contingencies.
Total project budget, maximum state grant and minimum local share were stated.
Town would finance roughly the local share over 30 years; the average household and higher brackets were given annual costs.
A renovation and addition would not be reimbursed and the town would lose committed state funding, and TC Passios would need to reopen.

budget_items.topic: Solar power purchase agreement at Turkey Hill
budget_items.what_was_said: Existing rooftop system under a power purchase agreement produces a share of the school's power and saves money annually.

budget_items.topic: New high school only and TC Passios repairs
budget_items.what_was_said: A new grade 9-12 high school was costed; keeping TC Passios open would need basic repairs, with renovation costing more.
Restoring a 50-year life cycle would be a large cost needed within about five years, starting with the roof.

decisions.decision: Board of Selectmen decided this week to finance the project over a 30-year term, after a survey in which about two-thirds preferred it.
Special town meeting set for January 7th and the debt exclusion ballot vote for Saturday the 11th.

what_happened.line: The School Building Committee held its third public forum on a new grade 6-12 middle-high school beside the current high school; no votes were taken.
The committee said the Board of Selectmen decided this week to finance the project over a 30-year term, after a survey in which about two-thirds preferred it.
The presentation covered the total project budget, the maximum state grant and the local share, with annual cost to an average household given as heard.
Presenters said a renovation and addition would not be reimbursed by the state, and that the town would lose committed state funding and need to reopen TC Passios.
A special town meeting was set for January 7th and the debt exclusion ballot vote for Saturday the 11th.

why_it_matters: The plan would be paid for through a debt exclusion, which adds to property tax bills for the length of the borrowing, so residents will be asked to vote on it at town meeting and at the ballot.
The state share applies only to the option the committee prefers, so the choice between building new and renovating changes both the local cost and whether other schools stay open.
watch_next: Debt exclusion ballot vote on Saturday the 11th.
